title: Finite-type algebra model of one affine base piece under further base change
statement: Let $S,T$ be schemes [def-pc-scheme], $d:T\to S$ affine, $X_0,Y_0$ schemes over $S$, and $f_0:X_0\to Y_0$ an $S$-morphism locally of finite type. Assume its base change $f_T$ is affine. Let $V\subset Y_0$ be affine and $W\subset S$ open with $V\subset Y_0^{-1}(W)$. Let $R$ be a commutative ring and $e_0:d^{-1}(W)\cong\operatorname{Spec}R$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. There exist commutative rings $B,C$, maps $a_B:R\to B$, $a_C:R\to C$, and a finite-type $R$-algebra map $\varphi:B\to C$ such that for every $t:L\to T$, commutative $R$-algebra $A$, and $e:t^{-1}(d^{-1}(W))\cong\operatorname{Spec}A$ compatible with $e_0$ and the algebra map $R\to A$, the base change of $f_0$ along $t\circ d$, restricted to the inverse image of $V$ under its target first projection, is isomorphic as an arrow to $\operatorname{Spec}(\mathrm{id}_A\otimes_R\varphi)$ [def-pc-fibre-product, lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra]. No inverse system or limiting cone is assumed.

source.place: Limits, proof of Tag 01ZO (lemma-descend-finite-finite-presentation), affine reduction; Schemes, Tags 01JR and 01I4; Morphisms, Tag 01T2.

proof.text: For Y_T=Y₀×_S T, X_T=X₀×_S T and f_T their induced map, the inverse image V_T of V is affine by affine base change; U_T=f_T⁻¹(V_T) is affine by affineness of f_T. Local finite type of f_T and its restriction follows from base change and restriction.

Set B=Γ(V_T), C=Γ(U_T), and q:V_T→d⁻¹(W) to be the restriction of the target second projection; its existence follows from hVW and the pullback condition. Put aB=(ΓSpecIso R)⁻¹ followed by (q followed by e0) on global sections; put aC=f_T|V_T on global sections composed with aB. This makes the latter ring map an R-algebra map φ. The affine-pairs criterion proves φ finite type. Naturality of isoSpec and the ΓSpec counit prove compatibility of the base map and φ with the spectrum presentations.
Apply the compatible-spectrum base-change lemma to these coordinate rings and the two naturality equations. This supplies all further base changes at once.

lean.statement: theorem exists_affine_base_piece_tensor_comparison {S T : Scheme.{u}} (d : T ⟶ S) [IsAffineHom d] (X₀ Y₀ : Over S) (f₀ : X₀ ⟶ Y₀) [LocallyOfFiniteType f₀.left] (haffine : IsAffineHom (((Over.pullback d).map f₀).left)) (V : Y₀.left.Opens) (hV : IsAffineOpen V) (W : S.Opens) (hVW : V ≤ Y₀.hom ⁻¹ᵁ W) (R : CommRingCat.{u}) (e0 : (d ⁻¹ᵁ W).toScheme ≅ Spec R) : ∃ (B C : CommRingCat.{u}) (aB : R →+* B) (aC : R →+* C), letI : Algebra R B := aB.toAlgebra letI : Algebra R C := aC.toAlgebra ∃ φ : B →ₐ[R] C, φ.FiniteType ∧ ∀ (L : Scheme.{u}) (t : L ⟶ T) (A : CommRingCat.{u}) (aA : Algebra R A), letI := aA ∀ (e : (t ⁻¹ᵁ (d ⁻¹ᵁ W)).toScheme ≅ Spec A), t.resLE (d ⁻¹ᵁ W) _ le_rfl ≫ e0.hom = e.hom ≫ Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap R A)) → Nonempty (Arrow.mk ((((Over.pullback (t ≫ d)).map f₀).left) ∣_ ((pullback.fst Y₀.hom (t ≫ d)) ⁻¹ᵁ V)) ≅ Arrow.mk (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (Algebra.TensorProduct.map (AlgHom.id R A) φ).toRingHom)))
